Four countries approve offshore wind capacity for 2026

Denmark approved 1200 MW of offshore wind this week, the largest single award the country has made. Germany approved 900 MW on the same day, and Poland approved 640 MW. Ireland approved 410 MW, completing the round.

Every figure in the round is stated in megawatts of nameplate capacity, which is what the joint announcement compares. None of the four regulators published the auction prices, and none said when construction is expected to begin.

The awards follow a joint statement signed last year, in which the four agreed to coordinate their auction calendars so that supply chains would not be asked to serve four separate peaks. Industry groups had argued that staggered rounds were raising the price of turbines and installation vessels for everyone in the sea basin.

Analysts cautioned that an award is not a connection. Grid operators in three of the four countries have open queues, and none of the announcements named a date by which the approved capacity is expected to reach customers. The joint statement says a progress review is planned, without saying who conducts it.

None of the four regulators would say whether a further round is planned. The statement commits them to publishing a shared progress report, and it does not say how often that report will appear or what it will contain.
